name: J. Scott Kirby

career.title: Budget analyst for the Secretary of Defense

background_rationale: An operations-research-trained analyst who spent three decades as an airline executive running network, revenue and operations as president of America West/US Airways, American and United before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Kirby drew criticism for remarks describing the traditional low-cost carrier business model as "dead," in a year when United also faced major operational disruptions at Newark.
Kirby said United would not pursue further merger deals, ruling out a consolidation push.
After oil prices spiked in March, United adjusted schedules to offset higher fuel costs and, reporting second-quarter revenue of $17.7 billion, raised its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $9.00-$11.00.
United announced 10 new international cities for 2027, which it called the largest international expansion in its history, along with the debut of the Airbus A321XLR.

personal_story.hook: Scott Kirby entered the Air Force Academy hoping to be a fighter pilot; he ended up running United Airlines.
personal_story.summary: Kirby grew up in Rowlett, Texas, the oldest of six children, and played baseball and football in high school with hopes of becoming a professional athlete. He arrived at the U.S. Air Force Academy aspiring to be a fighter pilot and graduated in 1989 with degrees in computer science and operations research. He began his career at the Pentagon as a budget analyst working alongside experienced economists, which shaped his analytical approach to problems, and later earned a master's in operations research from George Washington University. After working at airline-technology firm Sabre, he joined America West in 1995 and spent the next 25 years as an airline executive before becoming United's CEO in 2020.
